product_summary: A simple web-based expense tracking application that allows users to log in, record expenses, and view basic financial reports.
problem_statement: Individuals struggle to keep track of their daily expenses and lack visibility into their spending habits. There is a need for a lightweight, easy-to-use tool to log expenses and generate simple reports for personal financial awareness.
success_metrics: Number of active users logging expenses weekly
Average number of expenses logged per user per week
Time to first expense entry after signup

features.name: User Authentication
features.description: Users can sign up, log in, and log out securely.
acceptance_criteria: User can register with email and password
User can log in with valid credentials
Password is hashed and stored securely
Session is maintained after login
User can log out

features.name: Add Expense
features.description: Users can add a new expense with amount, category, date, and optional notes.
acceptance_criteria: Form includes fields for amount, category, date, and notes
Expense is saved to the database
Date defaults to current date
Category is selected from a predefined list

features.name: View Expense List
features.description: Users can view a list of their previously logged expenses.
acceptance_criteria: List displays amount, category, date, and notes
Expenses are sorted by date (newest first)
Each expense can be edited or deleted

features.name: Edit/Delete Expense
features.description: Users can modify or remove existing expenses.
acceptance_criteria: User can click edit to change expense details
User can delete an expense with confirmation
Changes are persisted in the database

features.name: Expense Reports
features.description: Users can view aggregated reports by category and time period (e.g., weekly, monthly).
acceptance_criteria: Bar or pie chart shows spending by category
User can select time range
Total spending for period is displayed
Data is filtered to current user only

features.name: Responsive Web Interface
features.description: Frontend is usable on desktop and mobile devices.
acceptance_criteria: UI renders correctly on mobile screens
Forms are accessible and easy to use on touch devices

user_flows.name: Log a New Expense
steps: Fill in amount, select category, confirm date, add notes

modules.name: Auth Module
modules.responsibility: Handles user registration, login, logout, and session management.

modules.name: Expense Module
modules.responsibility: Manages creation, retrieval, update, and deletion of user expenses.

modules.name: Reporting Module
modules.responsibility: Generates aggregated expense data for visualization.

modules.name: Frontend UI Module
modules.responsibility: Provides responsive web interface for user interaction.

suggested_tech_stack: Tailwind CSS or Bootstrap for styling
expected_scale: 10k DAU at launch, 100k DAU in year 1

data_entities.name: Expense
data_entities.description: Represents a single expense entry by a user.

data_entities.name: Report
data_entities.description: Aggregated view of expenses over time or by category.

possible_apis.description: List all expenses for the current user

functional_requirements: User must be authenticated to access expense and report endpoints
All expense operations are scoped to the authenticated user
Expense category must be one of predefined values (e.g., Food, Transport, Utilities, Entertainment, Health)
Reports must be generated in real-time or with minimal delay
Frontend must validate form inputs before submission

non_functional_requirements.description: API should respond within 500ms for 95% of requests under normal load
Passwords must be hashed using bcrypt or equivalent
System should be available 99.9% of the time
New users should be able to log first expense within 2 minutes of signup

constraints: Must be a web-only application (no native mobile apps initially)
Must support modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
assumptions: Users will access the app from personal devices
Initial user base will be tech-savvy early adopters
open_questions: Should we support expense attachments (e.g., receipts)?
Should reports support export to CSV/PDF?
Should we include budgeting features in future?
out_of_scope: Bank account integration or automatic transaction import
